 Samsung Galaxy Z Roll 5G: New Leaks Reveal 10-Inch Display and Possible 2028 Launch
 8:00 am November 3, 2026 By Roland Hutchinson 
 Samsung’s first rollable smartphone could represent one of the biggest changes to mobile device design in years. Following recent leaks about the company’s upcoming Galaxy Z lineup, new information has emerged about the possible Samsung Galaxy Z Roll 5G , also referred to as the Galaxy Z Slide , including its expandable display, innovative sliding mechanism, and potential release date.
 According to reports from South Korea, Samsung is developing a rollable smartphone that could feature an approximately 10-inch OLED display with a 16:9 aspect ratio . Unlike conventional foldable phones, which rely on hinges to open and close, the new device could use an expandable screen that slides out from the body, transforming a compact smartphone into a tablet-sized device.
 Recent leaks suggest that the Galaxy Z Slide could join Samsung’s smartphone lineup in 2027. However, earlier industry reports indicated that the company was targeting the first half of 2028 for its first commercial rollable smartphone.
 Although Samsung has demonstrated working rollable and slidable display technology, the company has not officially announced the Galaxy Z Slide or confirmed its final specifications.
 Key Takeaways
 New Galaxy Z Slide Leak: A recent leak suggests Samsung could introduce a rollable smartphone as part of an expanded Galaxy Z lineup in 2027.
 10-Inch Expandable Display: Industry reports point to a rollable OLED screen measuring approximately 10 inches when fully extended, with a 16:9 aspect ratio and a possible pixel density of 440ppi.
 Innovative Sliding Design: Samsung’s display demonstrations and patent filings reveal mechanisms that could allow a smartphone screen to expand without a traditional folding hinge.
 Potential Productivity Features: The expandable display could provide additional space for multitasking, video playback, document editing, and other productivity applications.
 Possible 2028 Launch: While recent rumours suggest a 2027 appearance, previous industry reporting points to the first half of 2028.
 Specifications Remain Unconfirmed: Samsung has not revealed the device’s processor, cameras, battery capacity, charging speeds, or pricing.
 Samsung Galaxy Z Slide Appears in New 2027 Lineup Leak
 One of the most interesting developments surrounding Samsung’s rollable smartphone emerged in October 2026, when tipster @TheGalox_ shared details about the company’s possible Galaxy Z lineup for 2027.
 According to the leak, Samsung could be preparing six devices, including the Galaxy Z Fold 9, Galaxy Z Fold 9 Pro, Galaxy Z Fold 9 Ultra, Galaxy Z Flip 9, Galaxy Z TriFold 2, and Galaxy Z Slide.
 The information, subsequently reported by 9to5Google and Android Authority , suggests Samsung could significantly expand its premium smartphone portfolio.
 The Galaxy Z Slide is particularly interesting because it could introduce an entirely different approach to expandable smartphone displays.
 Rather than unfolding a screen around a central hinge, the device would potentially extend its display horizontally or vertically, depending on the final design.
 However, the October leak does not provide detailed hardware specifications, and Samsung has not confirmed that the Galaxy Z Slide will launch in 2027.
 A 10-Inch Rollable OLED Display Could Transform the Smartphone Experience
 Expanding From Smartphone to Tablet
 One of the most significant reported features of Samsung’s upcoming rollable smartphone is its expandable OLED display.
 According to South Korean industry reporting, cited by SamMobile , market research firm Omdia expects the device to feature a display measuring approximately 10 inches when fully extended .
 The reported specifications include:
 Display Technology: Expandable rollable OLED panel.
 Expanded Screen Size: Approximately 10 inches.
 Aspect Ratio: 16:9.
 Pixel Density: Approximately 440 pixels per inch.
 Expansion Mechanism: A sliding or rolling display system, with the final implementation unconfirmed.
 A 10-inch display would provide substantially more viewing space than a conventional smartphone, potentially allowing users to switch between a compact mobile device and a larger workspace without carrying a separate tablet.
 The reported 16:9 aspect ratio could also make the expanded display particularly suitable for watching videos, viewing documents, and running multiple applications.
 The exact screen dimensions in the device’s compact configuration remain unknown.
 Could Samsung Finally Eliminate the Foldable Display Crease?
 Traditional foldable smartphones rely on flexible OLED panels that bend around a hinge. Although manufacturers have made significant improvements to foldable display technology, the crease remains a familiar characteristic of many folding devices.
 A rollable display takes a different approach.
 Instead of folding the screen in half, part of the flexible OLED panel is stored inside the smartphone’s body. When additional screen space is required, the display extends outward.
 This design could reduce the prominent central crease associated with conventional foldable phones.
 However, rollable technology introduces its own engineering challenges, including protecting the flexible panel, maintaining a smooth display surface, and ensuring that the extension mechanism remains reliable after years of use.
 Samsung has not confirmed whether its eventual rollable smartphone will feature a completely crease-free display.
 Samsung’s Latest Patents Reveal an Innovative Sliding Mechanism
 Samsung has been researching expandable smartphone displays for several years, and its patent filings provide some insight into the technologies the company is exploring.
 A Samsung patent published in August 2026 describes an electronic device with a display that expands through a sliding mechanism. The design includes structural components and guide assemblies intended to support the moving display.
 Another patent, highlighted by GSMArena , describes a rollable smartphone with an unusual movable camera module.
 In this design, the camera assembly moves alongside the expanding section of the device, potentially allowing Samsung to accommodate the camera hardware without interfering with the flexible display.
 The patent also discusses sensors that could detect changes in the display’s dimensions and the positions of internal components.
 These technologies could help Samsung address some of the challenges associated with expandable smartphone designs.
 However, patents represent technologies under consideration rather than confirmed commercial features. There is no guarantee that the Galaxy Z Slide will use either of these mechanisms.
 Samsung Has Already Demonstrated Working Rollable Displays
 While the Galaxy Z Slide remains unannounced, Samsung Display has already demonstrated several technologies that could help make a commercial rollable smartphone possible.
 Samsung Mobile Slidable
 At MWC 2026, Samsung Display demonstrated a Mobile Slidable concept featuring a screen that expanded vertically from approximately 5.1 inches to 6.7 inches.
 The demonstration illustrated how an expandable OLED panel could provide additional screen space while maintaining a compact form factor.
 Although this concept does not establish the final design of the Galaxy Z Slide, it demonstrates Samsung’s progress in developing flexible display systems.
 Samsung Rollable Flex
 Samsung Display previously introduced its Rollable Flex technology, demonstrating an OLED panel capable of expanding from approximately 49mm to more than 254mm.
 The technology uses a rolling mechanism to store part of the display before extending it into a significantly larger viewing surface.
 Samsung has also demonstrated its Flex Hybrid technology, which combines folding and sliding capabilities.
 These demonstrations highlight the company’s experience with expandable OLED displays, although the technologies have not all been incorporated into commercially available smartphones.
 Performance, Software, and Multitasking
 A smartphone capable of expanding into a tablet-sized device would require software that adapts smoothly to changing screen dimensions.
 Samsung already has considerable experience developing software for devices with multiple display configurations through its Galaxy Z Fold lineup.
 The company’s One UI interface supports features such as split-screen multitasking, floating windows, and application continuity on compatible foldable devices.
 A future rollable smartphone could build on these capabilities, potentially allowing applications to resize dynamically as the screen expands.
 Potential Productivity Features
 An expandable display could offer several practical advantages:
 Multitasking: Run multiple applications simultaneously across a larger workspace.
 Video Playback: Enjoy movies and streaming content on a tablet-sized display.
 Document Editing: Work with spreadsheets, presentations, and documents more comfortably.
 Web Browsing: Display more content without constantly scrolling or switching between applications.
 Gaming: Take advantage of additional screen space in compatible games.
 Samsung DeX and S Pen support would also be interesting additions to a rollable smartphone, particularly for productivity-focused users.
 However, neither feature has been confirmed for the Galaxy Z Slide, and current reports do not establish whether either will be included.
 Similarly, there are no reliable device-specific details about the processor, RAM, or storage configurations.
 Cameras, Battery Life, and Charging
 Samsung has yet to reveal the camera or battery specifications for its first rollable smartphone.
 The device’s expandable design could create additional challenges for internal component placement, particularly when accommodating a large battery, camera modules, and the mechanical components required to extend the display.
 Samsung’s patents suggest the company has explored different approaches to positioning cameras around moving display sections.
 However, there is currently no reliable information confirming the final camera resolution, lens configuration, or whether the device will feature an under-display camera.
 Battery life will also be an important consideration.
 A larger OLED display naturally requires additional power when fully extended, while the expansion mechanism may introduce further energy demands depending on its design.
 Samsung will need to balance battery capacity, device thickness, weight, and overall durability.
 For now, reports have not established the battery capacity, charging speed, or wireless charging capabilities of the Galaxy Z Slide.

 Samsung Galaxy Z Slide Release Date: 2027 or 2028?
 The potential release date remains one of the biggest unanswered questions surrounding Samsung’s first rollable smartphone.
 In June 2026, reports from South Korea suggested Samsung was targeting the first half of 2028 for the commercial launch of a rollable smartphone.
 According to the reporting, Samsung Electronics was working with Samsung Display on the project, although the final display supply arrangements had not been decided.
 More recently, the October 2026 Galaxy Z lineup leak included the Galaxy Z Slide among devices reportedly planned for 2027.
 There are several possible explanations for the conflicting information.
 Samsung may have accelerated its development schedule, the 2027 leak could refer to an earlier announcement rather than commercial availability, or the company’s plans may still be changing.
 It is also possible that the October leak is inaccurate.
 Until Samsung provides official confirmation, a release sometime in 2027 or 2028 remains speculative, with the first half of 2028 supported by earlier industry reporting.
 How Much Could Samsung’s First Rollable Smartphone Cost?
 Samsung has not announced pricing for the Galaxy Z Slide, and reliable device-specific pricing leaks have yet to emerge.
 Given the complexity of rollable OLED displays and the additional engineering required for an expandable smartphone, the device would likely be positioned within Samsung’s premium Galaxy Z portfolio.
 Its final price will depend on factors including display manufacturing costs, production volumes, internal hardware, and the reliability of the sliding mechanism.
 Early rollable smartphones could carry a substantial premium over conventional flagship handsets, particularly if production remains limited.
 However, any specific price estimate would currently be speculative.
 Is the Galaxy Z Slide the Future of Samsung Smartphones?
 Samsung’s work on rollable displays suggests that the company is exploring alternatives to traditional foldable smartphone designs.
 The potential advantages are compelling. A rollable device could combine the portability of a conventional smartphone with the additional screen space of a tablet, without requiring users to unfold a large display.
 However, several challenges remain.
 Samsung will need to ensure that the flexible OLED panel can withstand repeated expansion and retraction, that the internal mechanism is protected from dust and debris, and that the device remains practical in terms of thickness, weight, and battery life.
 Software optimisation will be equally important, particularly if Samsung wants applications to transition seamlessly between compact and expanded display modes.
 The latest reports suggest that Samsung’s rollable smartphone ambitions are progressing, but there is still a considerable difference between a working prototype and a mass-produced consumer device.
 If Samsung can overcome these challenges, the Galaxy Z Slide could become an important addition to its premium smartphone lineup and introduce a new category of expandable mobile devices.
 For now, the reported 10-inch display, Samsung’s continuing patent activity, and the appearance of the Galaxy Z Slide in recent leaks provide some of the clearest indications yet of what the company may be planning.
 Samsung has not confirmed the Galaxy Z Slide, and its final design, specifications, price, and release date remain unknown. 
 Frequently Asked Questions
 What is the Samsung Galaxy Z Roll 5G?
 The Galaxy Z Roll 5G is an unofficial name associated with Samsung’s rumoured rollable smartphone. More recent reports have referred to the device as the Galaxy Z Slide. Samsung has not confirmed either name.
 How big will the Galaxy Z Slide display be?
 Industry reporting suggests that Samsung is exploring an expandable OLED display measuring approximately 10 inches, with a 16:9 aspect ratio and a pixel density of around 440ppi. These specifications remain unconfirmed.
 When will the Samsung Galaxy Z Slide be released?
 Recent leaks suggest a possible appearance in 2027, while earlier South Korean industry reports pointed to a commercial launch during the first half of 2028. Samsung has not announced a release date.
 Will the Galaxy Z Slide have a crease?
 A rollable display could avoid the prominent central folding crease found on many conventional foldable smartphones. However, Samsung has not confirmed the final display design or whether the screen will be completely crease-free.
 Will the Galaxy Z Slide support the S Pen?
 There is currently no confirmation that Samsung’s rollable smartphone will support the S Pen. Compatibility will depend on the final display technology and digitiser implementation.
 How much will the Galaxy Z Slide cost?
 Samsung has not announced pricing, and there are no reliable device-specific pricing leaks. The device is likely to target the premium smartphone market if it reaches commercial production.
